UnitStatement: The appendix maps APEGA Relying on the Work of Others and Outsourcing requirements to the Chirality agent instruction architecture.
Each appendix mapping identifies the Chirality agent, invariant, file, or governed process that satisfies a regulatory requirement.
Each appendix mapping cites the governing document and section or invariant identifier for the mapped Chirality mechanism.
The appendix is intended to let regulators, auditors, or reviewing professionals trace compliance from regulatory text to architectural implementation.
PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md section 1.3 establishes the regulatory framework applied in the appendix.
AI agents producing work under a licensed professional direction are treated as others under APEGA section 3.0.
The firm obligations for AI-agent work engage direct supervision and control under APEGA section 3.1.1.
The firm obligations for AI-agent work engage thorough review under APEGA section 3.1.2.
Authentication obligations engage APEGA section 3.1 and Authenticating Professional Work Products.
APEGA section 3.1.1 requires a licensed professional relying on others work to provide direct supervision and control over that work.
Direct supervision and control is defined as directing, monitoring, and controlling engineering work throughout its lifespan.
Direct supervision and control includes making all decisions related to engineering practice.
Chirality satisfies APEGA direct supervision and control through gate-controlled orchestration.
Chirality satisfies APEGA direct supervision and control through the three-type agent hierarchy.
Chirality satisfies APEGA direct supervision and control through its invariant contract system.
APEGA section 3.1.1.1 identifies five specific obligations constituting active involvement.
Type 1 Manager agents operate through gate-controlled workflows.
In Type 1 gate-controlled workflows, the licensed professional makes consequential decisions at every phase transition.
Type 2 Specialist agents execute only within bounded briefs defined by the licensed professional or an authorized Type 1 agent.
Human authority is the halting condition in the workflow.
No agent may autonomously advance workflow stages, approve deliverables, or resolve conflicts.
Every agent instruction file declares the agent type, class, interaction surface, write scope, blocking behavior, primary outputs, and non-negotiable invariants.
Chirality architecturally enforces write scope.
No agent writes outside its declared zone.
The Type 0 Architect, Type 1 Manager, and Type 2 Specialist hierarchy establishes clear and non-overridable authority boundaries.
Authority flows downward and escalation flows upward in the three-type hierarchy.
Type 1 agents maintain interactive sessions with the licensed professional.
Type 1 agents present structured outputs and await human decisions at gates.
Type 2 agents receive INIT-TASK structured briefs and return structured run reports.
Type 2 structured run reports include PASS or FAIL status and recorded evidence.
NEXT_INSTANCE_STATE.md and NEXT_INSTANCE_PROMPT.md maintain session continuity without hidden state.
Deliverable working memory is maintained in _MEMORY.md.
AUDIT_AGENTS verifies agent instruction conformance against the canonical AGENT_HELPS_HUMANS standard.
Agent behavior is governed by workflow design requirements R1 through R9.
Agent behavior is governed by decomposition invariants I1 through I10.
Agent behavior is governed by 20 system-wide K-* invariants.
The evaluation framework systematically assesses agent output quality.
Agent instruction governance follows release engineering discipline.
Release engineering discipline for agent instruction governance requires versioning, review, and no silent behavior changes.
The REVIEW agent implements a formal 5-gate review process for all lifecycle transitions.
The RECONCILIATION agent performs cross-deliverable coherence analysis.
All agent outputs are git-committed to enable diff-based review at any point in the work history.
APEGA section 3.1.1.2 requires the licensed professional to be responsible for all technical engineering decisions.
_CONTEXT.md records identity and traceability for every deliverable.
_DEPENDENCIES.md records dependency summary for every deliverable.
_REFERENCES.md records source document pointers for every deliverable.
Structured deliverable context files are required structural elements of the project filesystem.
Technical direction is provided through agent briefs, explicit gate decisions, and conflict adjudication at human gates.
Licensed professionals are the mandatory decision authority at every gate.
Agents propose outcomes but do not declare outcomes.
No agent may bypass a gate or autonomously advance a workflow stage.
Interactive Type 1 sessions and gate-controlled workflows make the licensed professional a required participant in every consequential decision.
Type 2 agents cannot proceed without prior gate approval.
Outputs cannot advance to a new lifecycle state without human authorization.
Every decision is recorded in versioned files.
Decision Logs, _MEMORY.md, and _STATUS.md record durable decisions.
A decision not recorded in a versioned file does not exist for reliance purposes.
Agents are prohibited from maintaining hidden state that diverges from the filesystem.
APEGA section 3.1.1 requires the PPMP to describe the direct supervision and control process and associated record keeping.
PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md documents the complete direct supervision and control framework for AI agents.
PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md is referenced by the firm PPMP.
AGENT_*.md files document each agent scope, duties, authorities, and constraints.
Agent instruction files are part of the firm controlled quality system.
The controlled quality system requires agent instructions to be versioned, reviewed, and free of silent behavior changes.
The docs directory contains the firm full governance framework.
The governance framework includes DIRECTIVE.md, SPEC.md, TYPES.md, CONTRACT.md, and DBM_Agent_Instruction_Architecture.md.
Git history provides the complete development record of project state.
Git history records agent outputs, human decisions, and lifecycle transitions with diff-based traceability.
Timestamped append-only snapshot folders preserve analysis outputs.
No snapshot folder may be modified after creation.
APEGA section 3.1.2 requires thorough review before authentication of professional work products prepared by others.
Thorough review evaluates outputs sufficiently to verify reliability, validity, and technical accuracy.
Thorough review supports accepting professional responsibility for outputs.
Chirality satisfies thorough review through the REVIEW agent 5-gate protocol.
Chirality satisfies thorough review through the system epistemic labeling framework.
Chirality satisfies thorough review through the authentication gate structure.
APEGA section 3.1.2.1 specifies the substantive content of thorough review.
Scope of work is formally captured in _CONTEXT.md per deliverable.
Scope of work is confirmed at Gate 1 of the REVIEW agent 5-gate protocol.
The scope record is required and must be present before a review may proceed.
Risk assessments, operational conditions, and mitigation strategies are captured as governed deliverable content.
Findings related to risk adequacy are surfaced during Gate 3 of the review protocol with severity classification.
CRITICAL findings require human-resolved dispositions before an IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING transition is permitted.
Epistemic labeling requires non-trivial claims to be classified as FACT, ASSUMPTION, PROPOSAL, or TBD.
FACT means directly observed in source with citation.
ASSUMPTION means reasonable inference requiring validation.
PROPOSAL means agent suggestion requiring human decision.
TBD means unknown requiring resolution.
Assumptions are structurally visible rather than hidden in prose.
Suitability and local compliance are confirmed through the REVIEW agent Gate 2 checklist.
The Gate 2 checklist derives review items from deliverable specifications, decomposition records, and declared dependencies.
The licensed professional confirms checklist completeness at Gate 2 before review proceeds.
HSE findings are captured as CRITICAL severity findings in the REVIEW gate protocol.
CRITICAL HSE findings must be resolved before a deliverable may advance to CHECKING.
The hierarchy of authority places laws and regulations, including HSE requirements, as the first constraint.
The RECONCILIATION agent performs cross-deliverable coherence analysis across the project dependency graph.
Dependency registers are authoritative deliverable-local records.
Dependencies.csv captures inter-deliverable relationships with provenance.
Task-level agent outputs are captured in immutable snapshot folders.
Task-level snapshot folders include RUN_SUMMARY.md and QA_Report.md.
Task-level snapshots form the traceable evidence base for review.
Materials, methods, and construction requirements are captured within deliverable document kits.
Datasheet, Specification, Guidance, and Procedure formats make technical content documented and traceable.
The licensed professional must understand what each agent is instructed to do.
The licensed professional must understand what each agent output represents.
The licensed professional must understand how to verify agent outputs.
The licensed professional must understand LLM failure modes including hallucination, omission, and plausible-sounding error.
Chirality enforces tool competence as a prerequisite to reliance.
Technology provider due diligence is a documented firm obligation.
Technology provider due diligence includes evaluating model capabilities, limitations, safety practices, and model-update impacts.
Tasks admitting algorithmic validation are implemented as deterministic tools rather than left to LLM reasoning.
The tool registry indexes deterministic tools.
Interdisciplinary review obligations appear in the REVIEW Gate 2 checklist when cross-discipline dependencies are declared.
The RECONCILIATION agent identifies interface conflicts across discipline boundaries.
Every IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING lifecycle transition must traverse all five REVIEW gates.
Every CHECKING to ISSUED lifecycle transition must traverse all five REVIEW gates.
Gate 1 checks lifecycle state and context validity; the agent validates and the human confirms scope.
Gate 2 generates a checklist from specifications, decomposition records, and dependencies; the agent derives and the human confirms completeness.
Gate 3 captures findings iteratively; the human provides findings and the agent records evidence and severity classification.
Gate 4 disposition review requires humans to rule on all findings.
Gate 5 lifecycle transition decision has the agent recommend and the human approve.
IN_PROGRESS to CHECKING requires all CRITICAL findings to have a non-TBD human disposition.
CHECKING to ISSUED requires all CRITICAL findings to be RESOLVED.
CHECKING to ISSUED allows MAJOR findings only if they are RESOLVED or DEFERRED with documented rationale.
APEGA section 3.1.2.2 requires thorough review to verify compliance with the EGP Act and General Regulation.
APEGA section 3.1.2.2 requires thorough review to verify compliance with applicable APEGA practice standards, bulletins, and guidelines.
APEGA section 3.1.2.2 requires thorough review to verify contractual regulatory approvals or permit requirements.
The hierarchy of authority treats laws and regulations as the first constraint.
Agent instruction invariants enforce the hierarchy of authority.
Agents cannot override applicable legislation.
Regulatory compliance obligations flow to the licensed professional authenticating the professional work product.
The firm practice standard is grounded in APEGA practice standards identified in PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md section 1.1.
The firm practice standard maps the Chirality architecture to APEGA requirements.
Adherence to the firm practice standard is a condition of authentication.
Project-specific regulatory requirements are captured in _CONTEXT.md and _REFERENCES.md.
Compliance with project-specific regulatory requirements is a Gate 2 checklist item.
APEGA section 3.1.2.3 requires thorough review to verify that PWPs follow PPMP-defined QC and QA processes.
APEGA section 3.1.2.3 requires deliverables to be clear, readable, consistent, and complete.
PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md section 6 defines the firm complete QC and QA framework.
Architectural controls are implemented through six governance documents.
AUDIT_AGENTS verifies conformance of all agent instructions against the canonical standard.
Document kit format and required metadata structurally enforce deliverable clarity and completeness.
Epistemic labeling makes assumptions and TBD items conspicuous rather than hidden.
Agent instruction files are versioned in git.
Agent instruction files are reviewed before release.
Agent instruction files are subject to no silent behavior changes.
Material instruction changes to write scope, tool access, or outputs require a recorded release note.
Tasks admitting algorithmic validation are implemented as deterministic tools.
LLM probabilistic reasoning is confined to work requiring inference.
In the APEGA framework, authentication means a licensed professional represents completion, thorough review, or direct supervision and control and accepts professional responsibility.
Chirality implements authentication as a controlled gate.
Authentication is the final and irreversible human action in the lifecycle state machine.
Authentication is permitted only after direct supervision and control over AI-assisted work under professional practice standard section 4.
Authentication is permitted only after thorough review under professional practice standard sections 5.1 through 5.4.
Authentication additionally requires the conditions listed in section C.3.
The licensed professional must not use an AI agent to perform work they are not competent to verify manually.
An AI said so is never a defensible basis of design.
Competence to verify work is non-delegable.
The professional work product must be validated by the Responsible Member under the firm PPMP before authentication.
Authentication binds to a specific git SHA.
Content change after authentication voids the authentication.
A deliverable is dirty if any governed input has changed since its last approved SHA.
Merge to main is permitted only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA.
Only humans author binding approval records.
No agent may claim to certify, approve, sign, seal, or issue work for reliance.
The prohibition on agent authentication is an architectural invariant.
The licensed professional seal and signature apply to the specific version identified by the authentication SHA.
Content-addressed approval makes authentication integrity mechanically verifiable.
PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md section 2 maps APEGA statutory terms to Chirality agent system equivalents.
The definition mapping establishes terminology for the compliance analysis in sections C.1 through C.3.
All terms from APEGA practice standard section 1.3 apply throughout the professional practice standard.
A Licensed Professional is an individual entitled by the EGP Act to practise engineering in Alberta.
Chirality maps Licensed Professional to the P.Eng. operating the agent system and authenticating professional work products.
A Permit Holder is a partnership, association, or corporation holding a Permit to Practice under the EGP Act.
Chirality maps Permit Holder to Chirality AI Ltd., APEGA P17007.
A Responsible Member is an APEGA licensed professional responsible for oversight of the permit holder engineering practice.
Chirality maps Responsible Member to the firm registered Responsible Member, Ryan Tufts, P.Eng., APEGA 78780.
A Professional Work Product is an output of professional services with technical information relied upon for decisions or actions.
Chirality maps Professional Work Product to authenticated deliverables issued for reliance with lifecycle state ISSUED.
Authentication means a licensed professional completed, reviewed, or supervised and controlled work and accepts professional responsibility.
Chirality maps Authentication to human approval, seal, and signature at the issuance gate bound to a specific git SHA.
Validation means a Responsible Member reviewed the professional work product to ensure PPMP QC and QA measures are met.
Chirality maps Validation to Responsible Member review under the firm PPMP.
Direct Supervision and Control means directing, monitoring, and controlling engineering work, including all practice decisions.
Chirality maps Direct Supervision and Control to gate-controlled agent orchestration under the Type 0/1/2 hierarchy with human authority at every gate.
Thorough Review means evaluating professional-service outputs prepared by others to verify reliability, validity, and technical accuracy.
Chirality maps Thorough Review to the REVIEW agent 5-gate protocol plus the licensed professional authentication decision.
Due Diligence means reasonable judgment, care, forethought, and determination used to avoid harm to people, property, or environment.
Chirality maps Due Diligence to licensed professional judgment at every gate supported by the evidence trail.
The Chirality evidence trail includes provenance, epistemic labels, immutable snapshots, and git history.
An AI Agent is a controlled system architecture that performs bounded work under licensed professional direction.
AI Agent architecture includes model, instructions, tools, file access, and governance.
Chirality maps AI Agent to an AGENT_*.md instruction file instantiated at runtime in the agent operating system.
Agent Instruction Architecture is the firm framework of agent instructions, governance documents, invariant contracts, and deterministic tools.
Agent Instruction Architecture constitutes the direct supervision and control structure for AI agents.
Chirality maps Agent Instruction Architecture to the agents, docs, and tools directories governed by release engineering.
The K-* invariant cross-reference identifies the regulatory obligation served by each invariant.
The cross-reference enables regulators to verify that every catalog invariant has an identified regulatory function.
K-AUTH-1 states that only humans author binding approval records.
K-AUTH-1 prohibits agents from claiming to certify, approve, sign, seal, or issue work for reliance.
K-AUTH-1 serves authentication obligations under APEGA section 3.1 and Authenticating Professional Work Products.
K-AUTH-2 states that approvals bind to a specific git SHA.
K-AUTH-2 states that content change after approval voids approval.
K-AUTH-2 serves authentication integrity.
K-BIND-1 states that approvals are always binding and only binding.
K-BIND-1 serves authentication scope.
K-SEAL-1 prohibits Type 2 agent execution before context is sealed and gate-approved by a human.
K-SEAL-1 serves direct supervision and control.
K-GHOST-1 limits Type 2 agent context to folder contents and declared references.
K-GHOST-1 prohibits ghost inputs.
K-GHOST-1 serves scope documentation.
K-DEP-1 states that deliverable-local dependency files are authoritative.
K-DEP-1 serves cross-deliverable integrity.
K-DEP-2 requires dependency references to resolve to existing deliverable IDs.
K-DEP-2 serves traceability.
K-STATUS-1 declares _STATUS.md as the canonical lifecycle state file for each deliverable.
K-STATUS-1 serves record keeping.
K-STALE-1 propagates staleness from upstream changes to all transitive dependent deliverables.
K-STALE-1 serves change impact tracking.
K-STALE-2 requires stale items to be human-triaged before being considered current.
K-STALE-2 serves human decision authority.
K-VAL-1 treats a deliverable as dirty if any governed input changed since its last approved SHA.
K-VAL-1 serves authentication integrity.
K-GATE-1 makes gates dynamic per project instance.
K-GATE-1 establishes minimum gates of seal transition and pipeline run approval.
K-GATE-1 serves ongoing human involvement.
K-MERGE-1 allows merge to main only when branch HEAD equals the approved SHA.
K-MERGE-1 serves authentication integrity.
K-PROV-1 requires every extracted dependency row to cite evidence.
K-PROV-1 serves reliability, accuracy, and validity.
K-INVENT-1 requires unknown values to become TBD rather than guessed.
K-INVENT-1 serves reliability, accuracy, and validity.
K-CONFLICT-1 requires conflicts between sources to be surfaced, not silently resolved.
K-CONFLICT-1 serves reliability, accuracy, validity, and decision-making responsibility.
K-WRITE-1 requires every agent to have an explicit write scope.
K-WRITE-1 prohibits agents from writing outside their declared zone.
K-WRITE-1 serves scope and authority documentation.
K-SNAP-1 makes task agent output snapshots immutable.
K-SNAP-1 serves audit-trail record keeping.
K-HIER-1 states that projects are decomposed as packages containing deliverables.
K-HIER-1 serves scope documentation.
K-ID-1 states that deliverable IDs are stable and persist across path changes.
K-ID-1 serves traceability.
The appendix is part of a thesis examining Chirality agent instruction architecture as an AI governance framework for APEGA-regulated professional engineering practice.
The source for all APEGA requirements is Relying on the Work of Others and Outsourcing, May 2021 version 4.0.
The source for all Chirality mechanism citations is PROFESSIONAL_ENGINEERING.md Revision 1 dated 2026-03-29 and governance documents in docs and agents.
